findings.title: Second-pass retry in refreshModelCatalog is not exercised
findings.body: The test calls `refreshModelCatalog` twice after changing the manifest and asserts exactly one extra probe. That only checks the simple path: the first call probes and the second is a no-op. The `for (pass < 2)` loop exists for a pass that started before the fetch and recorded the old `updatedAt` (ProviderRegistry.ts:1088-1092). Nothing covers that case, so removing the second iteration would not fail the test. If you keep the loop, add an assertion with an in-flight `refreshAll` that captured the old manifest.

contracts.action: Opening the model picker (web) or the thread settings sheet (mobile) sends server.refreshProviders with modelCatalogOnly: true
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing explicit refresh: serverRefreshProviders with refreshModels / instanceId, which probes providers and returns a provider list (apps/server/src/ws.ts:2501-2553).
contracts.before_after: New path short-circuits in the handler, calls providerRegistry.refreshModelCatalog and returns { providers: [] }. The client onSuccess returns early when instanceId or cwd is undefined, so the empty list is not recorded as a workspace snapshot (packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts:1420-1424). The single-flight key includes modelCatalogOnly, so it does not collapse into other refreshes. Gated on the modelCatalogRefresh capability, so older servers that would ignore the field and probe every provider are not called.
contracts.visible_effect: New models appear in the picker through the config stream once the manifest changes and providers are re-probed. No spinner or error is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: Rejection is swallowed (reportFailure false, `void`). On the server, failures are caught by recoverRefreshFailure. The picker keeps the previous list, and the next open retries because probedManifestUpdatedAt is not advanced on a failed pass.

contracts.equivalent_path: ModelManifest.refresh (1h TTL, 5 min retry back-off) and forceRefresh.
contracts.before_after: It uses the same semaphore, settings gate (enableProviderUpdateChecks), retry back-off and stale-manifest rejection as refresh, and only the TTL differs (5 min). The fetch is bounded by FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS. refreshAll waits on provider probes, which this change does not bound, but the client call is fire-and-forget and the pass is detached.
contracts.visible_effect: At most one manifest fetch per 5 minutes per server regardless of how often pickers open. A full provider probe happens only when the manifest updatedAt differs from the last full pass.
contracts.failure_mode: If the fetch fails, the back-off returns the old manifest, updatedAt matches and nothing is probed.

summary: The change looks sound. The client only sends the new field to servers that advertise `modelCatalogRefresh`, and the client success handler ignores the empty `providers` result. The manifest fetch reuses the existing semaphore, back-off and settings gate. The probe loop handles a pass that started before the fetch. I found no defects. One minor test gap: the second-pass retry in `refreshModelCatalog` is not covered.
